meta.currencyBasis: Nominal INR per month, household level, approx. 2025-26 prices (extrapolated; see research/psychographics.md).
meta.notes: Traits are modelling parameters derived from cited evidence plus explicit assumptions. Shares are approximate agent-population weights by household within each region (sum to 1 per region). Not a statistical estimate.

traitDefinitions.riskAversion: 0-1. Willingness to give up expected return for certainty (0 = risk-neutral/seeking, 1 = extremely averse). 0.6 ~ Binswanger's 'moderate' class.
traitDefinitions.timePreference: 0-1. Present bias / effective discount rate (0 = very patient, 1 = spends windfalls immediately, borrows against future).
traitDefinitions.priceSensitivity: 0-1. Probability-weighted elasticity of switching seller/brand for a given price gap (1 = switches for ~1% saving).
traitDefinitions.socialConformity: 0-1. Weight on what kin, biradari/village or peer network does when choosing (crops, purchases, ceremonies).
traitDefinitions.statusConsumption: 0-1. Share of discretionary spending allocated to visible/positional goods (weddings, SUVs, kothis, phones).
traitDefinitions.brandLoyalty: 0-1. Persistence with the same brand OR the same trading partner (kiryana, arhtiya, dealer) across periods.
traitDefinitions.digitalAdoption: 0-1. Propensity to use UPI, e-commerce, app-based services; also speed of adopting new digital channels.
traitDefinitions.creditAppetite: 0-1. Willingness to borrow (formal or informal), including for consumption and ceremonies.
traitDefinitions.trustInInstitutions: 0-1. Trust in formal banks, insurers, government schemes and procurement relative to informal networks.
traitDefinitions.migrationAspiration: 0-1. Desire of the household to place a member abroad (or, for migrants, to keep circulating).
traitDefinitions.religiosity: 0-1. Weight of religious observance in time/spending (gurdwara/mandir donations, path, pilgrimages). MODELLING ASSUMPTION for all profiles; no Punjab-segment survey found.
traitDefinitions.lossAversion: Prospect-theory coefficient lambda (losses weigh lambda x gains); literature benchmark ~2.25 (Tversky & Kahneman 1992). Per-profile values are MODELLING ASSUMPTIONS.

profiles.name: Marginal farmer (<2.5 acres) with livestock and wage work
decisionRules: Grows wheat-paddy on all owned land; will not try a non-MSP crop unless an assured buyer exists
Sells paddy/wheat through the same arhtiya who advanced input credit; accepts deductions from payment
Buys groceries on monthly udhaar from village kiryana and settles after harvest (Apr-May, Oct-Nov)
Takes casual wage work (own or neighbours' fields, construction) in slack season
Cuts health and clothing spending first when a crop is lost; borrows informally for ceremonies rather than skipping them
triggers: crop loss from flood, pest or heat

profiles.name: Small farmer (2.5-5 acres), wheat-paddy with dairy
decisionRules: Sticks to wheat-paddy; plants paddy at the earliest permitted date
Uses a mix of cooperative-society/KCC credit and arhtiya advances; prioritises repaying arhtiya to keep the relationship
Hires custom combine and tractor services rather than owning; may lease in 1-3 acres if cash allows
Spends on private English-medium schooling and coaching if a child is seen as 'abroad material'
Matches village norms on wedding scale even when it requires borrowing

profiles.name: Medium landowning farmer (5-10 acres, semi-medium holding)
decisionRules: Sells paddy through same arhtiya every season even if a rival offers ~1% better terms
Owns a tractor (often financed); buys implements when neighbours do
Diversifies only partially (e.g., 1 acre maize/vegetables) when a buyback contract exists
Earmarks land-backed loans or sale of 1-2 acres to fund a child's study visa
Spends on visible items (SUV, house extension, wedding at a palace) after good harvests or remittance inflows
triggers: crop failure / heat stress on wheat
child's IELTS score or visa refusal

profiles.name: Large landowner (10+ acres) / arhtiya commission-agent family
decisionRules: Acts as lender: advances input and consumption credit to client farmers, recovered from mandi payments (15-18%+ p.a. reported)
Leases out part of land to smaller farmers or leases in from NRI-owned land
Invests surplus in land, urban plots, vehicles, and children's overseas education
Highly brand-conscious on vehicles, phones and wedding services; sets the local status benchmark
Lobbies collectively (arhtiya associations / farm unions) against procurement changes that bypass commission agents
triggers: change to arhtiya commission rate or direct-to-farmer payment

profiles.name: Landless Dalit (SC) agricultural and casual labour household
decisionRules: Income peaks in paddy transplanting (Jun-Jul) and harvests; borrows in lean months
Relies on Public Distribution System wheat and MGNREGA days when farm work is scarce
Borrows from employers, shopkeepers or relatives for illness and house repair before weddings (CRRID: illness 20%, house 24%, marriage 14% of debt)
Highly price-sensitive; buys small pack sizes and loose staples
Works for the same landowner families season to season, sometimes tied by advances
triggers: paddy mechanisation / direct-seeded rice adoption reducing labour days
caste-related social conflict over wages or village common land

profiles.name: Migrant labourer from UP/Bihar (seasonal or settled)
decisionRules: Remits a large share of earnings home (savingsRate here = share remitted/saved, not spent locally)
Arrives for paddy transplanting (Jun-Jul) and stays for harvest; leaves for home festivals and own harvests
Minimises local consumption: shared rooms, cooks own food, buys loose staples
Uses UPI mainly to send money home and receive wages from contractors
Negotiates per-acre piece rates as a group (toli) through a contractor
triggers: harassment or local hostility to migrants
crop timing shift in home state

profiles.name: Dairy-focused household (8-20 milch animals, 0-3 acres)
decisionRules: Sells milk to the same buyer (Milkfed/Verka society, private dairy or dodhi) on a 10-15 day payment cycle
Buys feed and mineral mixture on credit from the same dealer
Expands herd via bank/cooperative dairy loans when milk price is stable
Switches milk buyer for a higher fat-based price only after repeated payment delays

profiles.name: NRI-remittance household (member settled in Canada/UK/Australia/Gulf)
decisionRules: Leases out farmland (theka) rather than cultivating; land kept as security and status
Spends remittances on house construction/renovation, cars, furniture and loan repayment
Funds visa/fees for next family member; household network makes further migration easier
Peaks consumption during NRI visits (Dec-Feb) and weddings
Elderly parents left behind rely on paid help and private hospitals

profiles.name: Small-town trader / shopkeeper (Moga city, mandi towns)
decisionRules: Extends udhaar to regular farm-family customers and collects after harvest
Business revenue swings with harvest cash flow and NRI season
Accepts UPI (QR) for most sales but keeps cash for wholesale purchases
Responds to e-commerce competition by stocking branded fast-movers and offering home delivery

profiles.name: Aspiring student (IELTS/PTE, 17-24) in farm or trader household
decisionRules: Household income is the parents'; the agent controls coaching, test fees and phone/clothing spend
Retakes IELTS/PTE until target band is met; pays consultant (agent) fees
Family is willing to borrow, mortgage or sell land to fund fees and show funds
Switches destination country when a policy door closes (Canada -> Australia/UK/Germany)

profiles.name: Truck driver / owner-operator (1-2 trucks)
decisionRules: Income tied to grain movement after procurement seasons; idle time between
Truck financed by NBFC loan; EMI is the first claim on cash
Diesel price is the key cost; passes increases on with a lag
Considers driving abroad (Canada/US trucking) as a migration path

profiles.name: Rural youth (18-29) not in stable work
decisionRules: Lives in parental household; income above is household income, personal earnings are small and irregular
Spends personal money on mobile data, motorcycle fuel, clothing and socialising
Rejects farm labour seen as low-status but takes gig/driving/security jobs or govt recruitment exam prep
Small modelled probability of substance dependence, which raises spending on intoxicants and lowers household savings
triggers: govt recruitment drive (police, army Agniveer, teachers)

profiles.name: Central/State/UT government employee household
decisionRules: Stable salary on the 1st of each month; spending spikes around DA hikes and arrears
Prefers safe instruments: PF/NPS/UPS, FDs, LIC, property
Takes housing and car loans readily because income is secure
Shops at sector markets and malls; adopts UPI and online grocery

profiles.name: IT/ITES professional household (Mohali/Chandigarh IT Park)
decisionRules: Defaults to e-commerce and quick-commerce for groceries and electronics
Invests in equity mutual funds via SIP; tolerates market risk
Uses credit cards and buy-now-pay-later for big-ticket items
Keeps open option of onsite/overseas jobs

profiles.name: Business owner household (traders, manufacturers, professionals)
decisionRules: Income lumpy and cyclical; spends on visible status goods (cars, destination weddings)
Invests in property in tricity and Zirakpur/Kharar belt
Uses formal credit lines plus informal finance within community
Sends children abroad for study as a family strategy
triggers: local demand from Punjab farm economy

profiles.name: Retired government/defence pensioner household
decisionRules: Pension is income; salary key used for pension in this sim
Keeps savings in FDs, Senior Citizens Savings Scheme, post office; avoids equities
Very brand/shop loyal; slow to adopt new apps but uses UPI with family help
Health spending rises with age; children abroad may send support

profiles.name: University/college student (PU, PGIMER, private universities), living in PG/hostel
decisionRules: Income is transfer from parents ('remittance' key used for parental transfers)
Heavy UPI and app-based food delivery use
Very price-sensitive on food, but spends on phones and fashion for peer status
Considers foreign postgraduate study

profiles.name: Domestic / informal worker household (housemaids, construction, vendors)
decisionRules: Many are inter-state migrants who remit to native villages
Works for several employer households; wages paid monthly, often via UPI
Buys groceries on credit from local shops near colonies
Takes informal loans from employers in emergencies
